text: Every API call this whole course has been you calling a server. A webhook flips that completely: the server calls you, the moment something real happens. That's the whole idea, and it closes out chapter three.

Here's the real shape, straight from Stripe, and it's the same basic pattern you'll see from most webhook senders, AI providers included: an id, a type telling you what happened, and a data.object carrying the actual resource. One endpoint, many event types, a simple check on type.

But here's the catch: anyone who finds your webhook URL can POST fake JSON at it. So providers sign every real event. This is Stripe's actual signature header format — a timestamp, and an HMAC signature computed from that timestamp, the raw body, and a secret only you and the provider know. Verify it, or don't trust the payload.

So a solid webhook handler does three things in order: verify the signature before touching anything else, return a 200 immediately — don't make the provider wait on your slow database update — and only then do the real work, usually off on a queue.

Requests, responses, streaming, tool calls, errors, pagination, and now webhooks — that's the real shape of how AI provider APIs actually talk. Chapter four turns all of it into something you build yourself: a real API wrapper client.
